page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized enterprise instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. With 384 GB of system RAM, the instance maintains a consistent 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, delivering 8 GB of memory per individual vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering compute capability entirely on the dedicated Intel Xeon processor cores.

From an infrastructure and storage perspective, the ecs.r9i.12xlarge does not bundle local disk storage. All non-volatile data persistence must be provisioned via remote block storage volumes over the network. Networking throughput is defined by a baseline capacity of 25 Gbps, supporting significant data interchange across distributed clusters and remote storage infrastructure. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included, requiring external routing or associated gateway allocation for external connectivity.

In terms of qualitative resource efficiency, the provision of 8 GB of memory per core allows dense consolidation of memory-heavy tasks without over-provisioning compute resources. The dedicated vCPU architecture avoids shared-core contention, ensuring steady throughput for memory-bound execution. This hardware footprint is directly applicable to in-memory databases, large transactional relational databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and large-scale extract, transform, and load processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, the instance delivers 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 384 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-CPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The server operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include integrated hardware accelerators or local disk storage, depending on network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is backed by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With its dedicated compute allocation and substantial memory capacity, the instance offers balanced resource density for operations requiring large RAM working sets relative to execution threads. The hardware configuration targets in-memory caching systems, distributed memory caches, enterprise relational and non-relational database management, data mining, and large-scale enterprise application hosting.
